0.title: Course Introduction
0.content:
Congratulations on completing all of Level 2! Now it is time for the assessment. This quiz covers all the core knowledge you learned in Level 2: tuffeau geology, the Anjou-Saumur red wine group, the rosé spectrum, the Cabernet Franc triangle (Chinon / Bourgueil / Saumur-Champigny), the full picture of Touraine reds, and the influence of vessel type on winemaking style. Pass it, and the door to Level 3 — Chenin Blanc and flint — will open for you.

📝 Scope of assessment

All 8 lessons of Level 2 (lo-l2-1 to lo-l2-8), covering multiple red / rosé AOCs

🎯 Number of questions

5 comprehensive questions, covering geology, varieties, pairing and vessel craft

🏆 Pass mark

Answer 4 or more (80%) correctly to unlock Level 3
1.title: Level 2 Comprehensive Assessment
1.questions.0.question: What are the two key characteristics of tuffeau?
1.questions.0.options.1: Porous with good drainage + easy to dig into underground cellars
1.questions.0.options.3: Rich in volcanic minerals + suited to growing Gamay
1.questions.0.explanation: Tuffeau is a porous white limestone with excellent drainage for vine roots, and its soft texture makes it easy to dig into underground caves (caves), forming a natural cellar environment at a constant 12–14°C; it is the most important geological feature of Anjou-Saumur.
1.questions.1.question: Which is the most famous legendary estate of Saumur-Champigny?
1.questions.1.options.0: Charles Joguet (a fine-wine estate of Chinon)
1.questions.1.options.1: Clos Rougeard (the Foucault brothers, long ageing in oak barrels)
1.questions.1.options.2: Domaine de Bellivière (natural wine of the Loir valley)
1.questions.1.options.3: Domaine de la Chevalerie (a traditionalist of Bourgueil)
1.questions.1.explanation: Clos Rougeard (founded by the Foucault brothers, now part of the Bouygues group) is Saumur-Champigny's most legendary estate, ageing for a long time in oak barrels (Le Bourg in brand-new, heavily toasted new barrels); its top wine Le Bourg is priced very high on the second-hand market and is called "the Romanée-Conti of the Loire."
1.questions.2.question: Why is Touraine-Noble-Joué one of France's most unusual rosé AOCs?
1.questions.2.options.0: It is the only Loire rosé allowed to add sugar
1.questions.2.options.1: It mandates a blend of three Pinot varieties (Pinot Meunier + Pinot Gris + Pinot Noir)
1.questions.2.options.2: It can be made only once a year, with harvest on a fixed date
1.questions.2.options.3: It is France's only rosé AOC allowing only Cabernet Franc
1.questions.2.explanation: Touraine-Noble-Joué mandates a blend of three Pinot-family varieties (Pinot Meunier, Pinot Gris, Pinot Noir), creating a unique "grey rosé (vin gris)" style with over 500 years of history, once the royal table wine of the French court in Touraine.
1.questions.3.question: What is the most signature aroma of Pineau d'Aunis, and in which sub-region is it mainly planted?
1.questions.3.options.0: Honey and apricot, mainly in Vouvray
1.questions.3.options.1: White-pepper spice + violet, mainly in the Loir valley (Coteaux-du-Loir) and Vendômois
1.questions.3.options.2: Blackcurrant and cedar, mainly in Chinon
1.questions.3.explanation: Pineau d'Aunis is known for white-pepper spice and violet florals; it is the Loire's most distinctive native variety, planted almost only in the Loir valley (Coteaux-du-Loir) and Coteaux-du-Vendômois of the southern tributaries, and extremely rare elsewhere.
1.questions.4.question: Of Chinon's three soil types, which "light, high-acid, low-tannin" style best cuts the rich fat of Rillettes de Tours?
1.questions.4.options.0: Plateau clay-limestone (plateau) — the firmest tannins, the best match for fat
1.questions.4.options.1: Tuffeau slopes (coteau) — firmer structure, needs ageing, better with large red meat such as leg of lamb
1.questions.4.options.2: Gravel flats (graviers) — light and fresh, high acidity, the best fat-cutting effect
1.questions.4.options.3: None of the three suits it; drink white instead
1.questions.4.explanation: Chinon from gravel flats (graviers) is the lightest and has the crispest acidity, effectively cutting the rich fat of rillettes, and when drunk young its strawberry and violet fruit makes a sweet–salty contrast with the salty meat. Chinon from tuffeau slopes and plateau clay-limestone has firmer structure and suits richer meats such as leg of lamb better.
